abstract: For Beurling zeta functions zeta = exp(int x^{-s} dm) with dm >= 0 and regular growth functions with limsup log psi/phi <= kappa, the best constant c*_reg(kappa) in Landau's zero-free region lies in [sup_a N_a/(S_a + kappa), 0.4124] for 0 < kappa <= 1. The lower end comes from frequency-dependent kernels (Paper 98) and tends to about 0.103 as kappa -> 0; the upper end comes from explicit constructions (Papers 93, 97). Paper 93 (Sec. 7, Remark 3) asks whether the two methods meet. We drop the integrality of zero multiplicities and keep the rest: dm >= 0, a non-negative zero measure, unit mass at the designated zeros, and no zero mass asymptotically closer to the 1-line than they are. In the scaling limit of Paper 93 with K clusters, the relaxed construction problem is a linear programme in profile functions. We prove that its threshold P_K equals the value of the kernel programme of Paper 98 with positive definiteness imposed on the first K harmonics, and that P_K decreases to the supremum L* of the constant N_a/S_a of Paper 98 over all admissible kernels. Numerically L* is about 0.1029 (an extrapolation), and 0.1027 < L* <= 0.115, the upper end by a floating-point check with explicit error terms. If the lifting criterion of Paper 93 extends to diffuse zero mass (not proved here), and the proof of Paper 97 extends to it (also not proved here), then the relaxed constant tends to L* as kappa -> 0+. Near kappa = 0, no argument that uses only these positivity conditions can then give a constant above L*; a better constant would have to use structure the relaxation discards, such as integrality. Nothing here concerns the zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
Revision answering the acceptance review of version 1. No theorem, proof step or numerical value changes.
(1) The extension of [97] to diffuse zero mass is now stated as Hypothesis (Q), alongside Hypothesis (L). The status line, abstract, Section 1, Remark 7.3 and Section 6 say that the statement about c*_rel depends on (L) and (Q), and that a constant above L* would have to use structure the relaxation discards; no gap for the original class is claimed.
(2) "Rigorously certified" is replaced by "checked in floating point with explicit error terms". cert_check.py (v2 in the supplement; v1 kept as cert_check_v1.py) now bounds the second-derivative integral by an upper Riemann sum instead of the trapezoid rule, adds a roundoff bound, and includes the e^{tau h} factor in the angular error. All margins stay positive; the smallest is 3e-5 (K = 3, constraint B1), the others are at least 1.9e-4. The text says this is not a validated-arithmetic certificate. Theorems 1 and 2 do not depend on it.
(3) L* ~ 0.1029 is labelled an extrapolation; the proved bounds are 0.1027 < L* <= P_6 <= 0.115, the last as in (2).
(4) Definition 3.1: D_K and D_infinity take the supremum over kernels with 0 < S < infinity.
(5) Theorem 1: Luenberger is a numbered reference [Lu69, Sec. 8.6, Thm 1], and the framework is stated (the vector space of profiles, Z = C(Omega_K) with its positive cone having interior, affine constraint maps, dual space of signed Radon measures).
(6) [93] is cited as v2 (Section 7, Remark 3). Broucke arXiv:2507.13780, Mossinghoff-Trudgian-Yang arXiv:2212.06867 and Broucke-Revesz arXiv:2611.03356 are cited in the literature paragraph; Remark 7.3 notes that [BR26, Sec. 6] already improves a Landau constant with a second zero from a clustering theorem, a step that uses integrality of zero counts.
title: Without integrality, constructions and kernels for Landau's theorem have the same value
